findings.title: Family reputation as an evidentiary frame
findings.claim: The sister, father, and mother sequence frames family reputation as the public test being applied to an individual's conduct, while the two negated predicates expose that lineage-based test as an unsound proof.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers for sisterhood, fatherhood, mothering, badness, and sexual transgression contact distinct supplied wider scenes of lineage attribution, public slander, and accusation. Together those contacts change the reading from two isolated character denials into a rebuttal of genealogy being used as evidence of an individual's act.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the kinship panel comes before the paired denials: the verse is answering a family-based case against the individual, not merely listing the parents' virtues.
findings.containment: The literal public address and both negations remain intact. This does not settle the historical relation intended by the sister-address, make any target wording a lexical equivalent of a focus word, or treat target-side connections without supplied morphology as certainty.

epistemic.reason: The supplied cross-run finding and its focus branch records are trusted and the five carriers are exact. The wider connections supply exact target Arabic but no target morphology, so the cross-ayah mechanism is retained as qualified contextual evidence.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening address becomes the first element in a genealogy-based case whose asserted relation is itself under scrutiny.
branch_activations.boundary: This retains the literal sisterhood relation and does not decide the historical identity or exact relation meant by the address.

findings.title: Maternal origin behind the public label
findings.claim: The maternal carrier can also make the public family test reach back to the source of Mary's named identity, not only to the moral character of a parent.
findings.mechanism: The focus's mother noun contacts 3:36, where the supplied Arabic presents the mother naming Mary and seeking protection for her and her offspring. That separate maternal source scene activates the root's origin facet and changes the denial panel into a test of the origin being invoked as evidence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive a second pressure in the mother reference: the accusation reaches toward the origin of the person being judged, while the verse still denies the alleged conduct.
findings.containment: The literal mother relation and the family-reputation finding remain primary. This is a bounded origin resonance, not a claim that the mother causes Mary's status or that the target supplies focus-word morphology.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and target Arabic are supplied exactly, but the connection is a contextual nomination and target morphology is absent; the origin facet is therefore retained as qualified rather than lexical certainty.

findings.title: Badness as reputational harm
findings.claim: The focus's badness quality can also register the harm inflicted by a public false charge, giving the denial a concrete injury dimension alongside its moral characterization.
findings.mechanism: The genitive سَوْءٍ carrier contacts 33:58, whose supplied Arabic condemns harming believers with what they did not earn as slander and manifest sin. The separate harm scene supplies an act and consequence for the focus quality, changing it from an abstract label into a bounded image of injury done by accusation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees that denying the father's badness also answers the damage done by attaching a bad name to the family, not just the abstract question of virtue.
findings.containment: The focus does not assert a transitive harm event, and سَوْءٍ is not equated with the target's slander vocabulary. The ordinary moral-quality reading remains recoverable and target morphology is absent.

epistemic.reason: The focus form and target Arabic are exact, but the harm facet is a contextual extension and the target connection lacks supplied morphology; it is therefore explicitly qualified.

findings.title: The accusation itself crosses the boundary
findings.claim: The focus's negated sexual-class predicate can also expose the act of imposing the charge as an overstepping, rather than leaving the charge as a neutral description.
findings.mechanism: The بَغِيًّا carrier contacts 24:4, where the supplied Arabic requires witnesses for accusing chaste women and brands unsupported accusers false. That independent evidentiary trigger activates the root's boundary-crossing facet and shifts the reading so the accusation itself becomes morally accountable.
findings.reader_payoff: The final denial can be felt as a reversal of the public charge: the stigma is rejected, and the unsupported act of attaching it is placed under scrutiny.
findings.containment: The sexual-class predicate remains the focus's ordinary denied reading. This does not make بَغِيًّا a synonym for the legal accusation terms, and target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and the exact target Arabic are supplied, while the branch activation depends on a contextual connection whose target morphology is absent; the resulting overstep reading remains qualified.
